title: How do you feel?
summary: A reflexive verb has a pronoun that points back to the subject: ik voel me, jij voelt je, hij voelt zich, wij voelen ons. It stands after the verb, or after the subject when that follows the verb or in a sub-clause. Perfect: with hebben.
explain:
A reflexive verb (*een wederkerend werkwoord*) has an extra pronoun that refers back to the subject: `Ik vergis me` (I am mistaken), `Hij voelt zich goed` (he feels well). The pronoun does not add a person; it is the subject itself. Many verbs about feelings and daily care work this way.

### The reflexive pronouns

| | zich voelen |
| ik | voel me |
| jij / je | voelt je |
| u | voelt zich / voelt u |
| hij, zij / ze, het | voelt zich |
| wij / we | voelen ons |
| jullie | voelen je |
| zij / ze | voelen zich |

- Only `zich` is a new word. The others look like object pronouns, but with **jij** and **jullie** it is `je`, never jou, and not jullie either: `Jij voelt je`, `Jullie voelen je`. (Only in an order to a group is `jullie` also right: `Draai jullie om` or `Draai je om`.)
- With `ik` you will also read `mij` (`Ik voel mij goed`); in speech `me` is normal.
- With `u` both `zich` and `u` are correct: `U vergist zich` or `U vergist u`. `zich` is more usual.

> Ik voel me vandaag niet zo goed. — I don't feel so well today.
> Mijn oma voelt zich soms eenzaam. — My grandmother sometimes feels lonely.
> Wij verheugen ons op het weekend. — We are looking forward to the weekend.

### Always reflexive

Some verbs always have the pronoun when they have the meaning given here. Learn them with `zich`:

`zich vergissen` (to be mistaken), `zich schamen` (to be ashamed), `zich haasten` (to hurry), `zich herinneren` (to remember), `zich vervelen` (to be bored), `zich zorgen maken` (to worry), `zich verheugen op` (to look forward to), `zich ergeren aan` (to be annoyed by), `zich afvragen` (to wonder), `zich voorstellen` (to introduce yourself, to imagine).

`zich voelen` belongs here when it is about how you feel: `Ik voel me moe`. Without the pronoun, `voelen` means to touch or notice something: `Ik voel de wind`.

### Sometimes reflexive

Other verbs can have an ordinary object or the reflexive pronoun. Use the pronoun when the action goes back to the subject: `wassen`, `aankleden`, `scheren`, `omdraaien`, `verstoppen`.

> Ik was de baby. Daarna was ik me. — I wash the baby. Then I wash myself.
> Hij kleedt zich snel aan. — He gets dressed quickly.

`Hij wast hem` means that he washes someone else. For himself it must be `zich`.

### Word order

The pronoun stands **directly after the conjugated verb**. When the subject comes after the verb, the pronoun comes after the subject. In a sub-clause it follows the subject. Only a short `het` comes before it: `Ik herinner het me niet` (I don't remember it).

> Morgen voel je je vast beter. — You will surely feel better tomorrow.
> Ik denk dat ze zich verveelt op school. — I think she is bored at school.

With a modal verb or in the perfect, the pronoun stays in the middle and the other verb goes to the end. The perfect of a reflexive verb is made with `hebben` (for every verb in this unit; a rare exception like `Ik ben me doodgeschrokken` comes much later):

> Jullie moeten je haasten. — You have to hurry.
> Ik heb me vergist in de datum. — I made a mistake about the date.

### Watch out

- **Do not drop the pronoun**: *Ik herinner die dag → `Ik herinner me die dag`.
- **jij and jullie take je**: *Jij voelt jou niet goed → `Jij voelt je niet goed`.
- **Not hem or haar for himself or herself**: *Mijn vader scheert hem → `Mijn vader scheert zich`.
- **hebben, not zijn**: *Ik ben me vergist → `Ik heb me vergist`.
- **Pronoun after the subject** in inversion: *Morgen voel me ik beter → `Morgen voel ik me beter`.

`elkaar` means "each other" and is not the same as `zich`: `Ze zien elkaar morgen` (they see each other), `Ze wassen zich` (they wash themselves).

### Compared with Ukrainian

Ukrainian -ся and Dutch `zich` often do not match. These Ukrainian verbs are **not** reflexive in Dutch: сміятися = `lachen`, вчитися = `leren`, повертатися = `terugkomen`, сподіватися = `hopen`. And the other way round: пам'ятати has no -ся, but Dutch says `zich herinneren`. Learn every Dutch verb with or without `zich`, and do not translate the -ся.

words.en: to be mistaken / to make a mistake

sentences.nl: Ik voel me vandaag niet zo goed.
sentences.en: I don't feel so well today.
sentences.note: With ik the reflexive pronoun is me. It stands directly after the verb voel.
alt: Vandaag voel ik me niet zo goed.
Ik voel mij vandaag niet zo goed.
Vandaag voel ik mij niet zo goed.

sentences.nl: Mijn oma voelt zich soms eenzaam.
sentences.note: Mijn oma is a hij/zij-subject, so the pronoun is zich: the only reflexive pronoun that is a word of its own.
alt: Soms voelt mijn oma zich eenzaam.

sentences.nl: Morgen voel je je vast beter.
sentences.en: You will surely feel better tomorrow.
sentences.note: The first je is the subject, the second the reflexive pronoun. Morgen comes first, so the subject follows the verb and the pronoun follows the subject.
alt: Je voelt je morgen vast beter.
Morgen voel jij je vast beter.
Jij voelt je morgen vast beter.

sentences.nl: Mijn broer ergert zich aan het lawaai van de buren.
sentences.en: My brother is annoyed by the neighbours' noise.
sentences.note: zich ergeren aan (to be annoyed by) has both the pronoun and the preposition aan. Zich stands right after ergert.

sentences.nl: Maak je geen zorgen, het komt goed.
sentences.en: Don't worry, it will be all right.
sentences.note: An imperative of a reflexive verb: maak + the pronoun je for the person you speak to. Zorgen has no article, so the negative is geen.
alt: Maak je geen zorgen, het komt wel goed.

sentences.nl: Herinnert u zich die dag nog?
sentences.en: Do you (formal) still remember that day?
sentences.note: In the meaning 'to remember', herinneren always has the pronoun, unlike Ukrainian пам'ятати. With u the pronoun is zich (u is also correct).
alt: Herinnert u u die dag nog?

sentences.nl: Ik heb me vergist in de datum.
sentences.en: I made a mistake about the date.
sentences.note: The perfect of a reflexive verb is made with hebben. The pronoun me comes straight after heb, and the participle vergist goes to the end.
alt: Ik heb me in de datum vergist.
Ik heb mij vergist in de datum.
Ik heb mij in de datum vergist.

sentences.nl: Ik denk dat ze zich verveelt op school.
sentences.en: I think she is bored at school.
sentences.note: In a sub-clause with dat the verb goes to the end, and the pronoun zich stays directly after the subject ze.
alt: Ik denk dat zij zich verveelt op school.
Ik denk dat ze zich op school verveelt.
Ik denk dat zij zich op school verveelt.

sentences.nl: Jullie moeten je haasten, de trein vertrekt zo.
sentences.en: You (plural) have to hurry, the train is leaving in a moment.
sentences.note: With jullie the reflexive pronoun is je, not jullie. With a modal verb the pronoun stays after moeten and the infinitive haasten goes last.

sentences.nl: Hij wast zich en kleedt zich snel aan.
sentences.en: He has a wash and gets dressed quickly.
sentences.note: wassen and aankleden can also take another object (hij wast de auto). Here the action goes back to him, so zich, never hem.
alt: Hij wast zich en hij kleedt zich snel aan.

exercises.note: The reflexive pronoun for ik is me (in writing also mij). Zich is only for hij, zij, het, u and plural zij.
He shaves himself, so the pronoun points back to the subject: zich. Hem would be another man.

exercises.en: We are looking forward to the weekend.
exercises.note: With wij the reflexive pronoun is ons. Onze is a possessive (our) and needs a noun after it.

exercises.nl: Ik ___ dat het morgen mooi weer wordt.
exercises.en: I hope the weather will be nice tomorrow.
exercises.note: hopen is not reflexive in Dutch, although Ukrainian says сподіватися with -ся. Do not translate the -ся.

exercises.nl: Ik ___ me in het weekend goed ontspannen.
exercises.en: I relaxed well at the weekend.
exercises.note: Reflexive verbs form the perfect with hebben: ik heb me ontspannen. Ontspannen is also the participle.

exercises.nl: Jij voelt ___ vandaag niet lekker, hè?
exercises.en: You are not feeling well today, are you?
exercises.note: The reflexive pronoun for jij is je. Jou is never used as a reflexive pronoun.
The reflexive pronoun for jullie is je, the same as for jij. Not jullie.
With u the reflexive pronoun is zich or u; both are correct, zich is more usual.

exercises.nl: Draai ___ even om, ik wil de achterkant van je jas zien.
exercises.en: Turn round for a moment, I want to see the back of your coat.
exercises.note: An imperative to someone you say jij to: draai + je. The prefix om goes to the end.

answers: Voor een examen voel ik me altijd zenuwachtig.
exercises.en: Before an exam I always feel nervous.
exercises.note: Voor een examen takes the first place, so the verb comes next and then the subject. The pronoun me follows the subject ik.

answers: Ik denk dat hij zich vergist.
exercises.note: In the sub-clause the verb vergist goes to the end; zich stays directly after the subject hij.

answers: Gisteren heb ik me erg geërgerd aan de buren.
Gisteren heb ik me erg aan de buren geërgerd.
exercises.en: Yesterday I was very annoyed by the neighbours.
exercises.note: After Gisteren comes heb, then ik, then me. The phrase with aan may stand before or after the participle.
The perfect of a reflexive verb is made with hebben. The pronoun stays after the conjugated verb heb.

exercises.task: The action now goes back to the subject: replace de kinderen by the reflexive pronoun.
exercises.note: aankleden can take an ordinary object or a reflexive pronoun. For ik the pronoun is me, and aan still goes to the end.

answers: Dat heb ik me ook afgevraagd.
Dat heb ik mij ook afgevraagd.
exercises.note: zich afvragen always needs the pronoun, also in the perfect with hebben. Dat comes first, so ik follows heb and me follows ik.

exercises.wrong: Mijn zoon leert zich Nederlands op school.
answers: Mijn zoon leert Nederlands op school.
Mijn zoon leert op school Nederlands.
exercises.en: My son is learning Dutch at school.
exercises.note: leren is not reflexive, even though Ukrainian says вчитися. The pronoun zich has to go.
